title: Is This Agentic AI? One-Minute Decision Card
summary: Classify an exact AI experience by observable control flow instead of a provider, model, assistant, copilot, or agent label.
prerequisites: Name the exact product surface, version, configuration, and observed run
Separate the model from the interface, tools, state, policy, and runtime

accessibility.plainLanguageSummary: Ask who chooses the next step, who executes tools, what state persists, and who can stop the run.
accessibility.nonColorCues: Every outcome uses a class name and observable-signal list; color is never the only cue.
accessibility.reducedMotionAlternative: Present the complete decision tree as an ordered text list with no animated transitions.

sections.title: Freeze the unit before naming the class
paragraphs: Do not ask whether an entire provider or model family is agentic. Record the exact experience, version, configuration, tools, permissions, and observation date. The same model can appear in a one-call endpoint, a fixed workflow, or a tool-running agentic harness.

If the boundary is not observable, classify the claim as unknown. A product name, natural-language conversation, multiple turns, or a returned tool-call object does not prove execution, durable state, feedback, or autonomous continuation.

sections.title: Follow the observable control flow
paragraphs: A model maps supplied input to output. A deterministic workflow follows code-owned transitions. An agent has a bounded goal and model-directed next-step choice. An agentic system adds the runtime, tools, state, policy, telemetry, evaluation, recovery, and accountable people around one or more agents.

Ask five questions in order: who chooses the next step, who executes a proposed action, who owns durable state, who decides to stop or recover, and which human or deterministic control retains final authority.

code.label: One-minute classification record
code.code:
Task: [CLASSIFY ONE EXACT EXPERIENCE]
Scope: [SURFACE, VERSION, CONFIGURATION, TOOLS, AND OBSERVATION DATE]
Permissions: [READ, WRITE, NETWORK, DATA, AND APPROVAL BOUNDARIES]
Evidence: [NEXT-STEP CONTROLLER, EXECUTOR, STATE, FEEDBACK, STOP, AND HUMAN CONTROL]
Authority: [WHO MAY APPROVE EFFECTS AND FINAL CLASSIFICATION]
Decision: [MODEL | ASSISTANT | TOOL-CALLING MODEL | DETERMINISTIC WORKFLOW | AGENT | AGENTIC SYSTEM | MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM | UNKNOWN]
Stop conditions: [MISSING BOUNDARY, UNSUPPORTED CLAIM, OR UNVERIFIED SIDE EFFECT]
Verification: [TRACE ONE RUN AND LINK EACH SIGNAL TO DOCUMENTED OR TESTED EVIDENCE]
Recovery: [WITHDRAW THE CLAIM, PRESERVE UNKNOWN, AND REQUEST THE MISSING EVIDENCE]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence is a dated system boundary, an observable transition trace, tool-execution and side-effect evidence, state ownership, stop and recovery behavior, and the accountable reviewer. Label each claim documented, tested, inferred, or unknown.

Verify the classification against at least one plausible neighboring class. Stop publication if a critical boundary is unknown or if a marketing label is doing the work of evidence. Recover by narrowing the claim to the exact behavior the evidence supports.
